description: AstraVitals is a team exploring how space science and data can help improve human health. Competing in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we bring curiosity, creativity, and a shared drive to turn complex challenges into practical solutions. Our mission is to connect discoveries beyond Earth with healthier lives on it.
summary:
ASTRAVITALS is an end-to-end biomedical telemetry and autonomous clinical decision-support console engineered for human spaceflight missions in Low Earth Orbit and deep space. We developed a full-stack system combining a Python/Flask IoT telemetry ingestion and data-cleaning pipeline, a PostgreSQL time-series database, a Java Spring Boot backend, and a real-time clinical dashboard.

The platform addresses spaceflight health challenges by continuously monitoring four critical physiological domains—Cardio, Bone, Behaviour, and Radiation—while automatically filtering sensor outliers and imputing missing readings. Its integrated EVA Go/No-Go engine cross-checks multi-system thresholds before clearing extravehicular activities, while an ISS/Mars latency mode simulates light-time communication delays (0.2 seconds vs. 14+ minutes) to activate onboard autonomous triage and printable Flight Surgeon briefs when ground control cannot respond in real time.

ASTRAVITALS is vital for future Artemis and Mars expeditions, where communication delays make Earth-dependent medical care dangerous. By shifting clinical decision-making directly onboard, it safeguards astronaut health during deep-space missions and provides a resilient telemedicine framework for isolated, low-bandwidth environments on Earth.
details:
ASTRAVITALS is a full-stack biomedical telemetry platform and autonomous clinical decision-support console engineered for human spaceflight missions in Low Earth Orbit (ISS) and deep space (Lunar/Mars transit). The system operates through a four-tier pipeline:

  1. IoT Telemetry Ingestion & Self-Healing Pipeline (python-service/app.py): A Python/Flask ingestion server receives real-time JSON biometric packets from simulated ESP32 wearable sensors. Every incoming reading is validated against physiological bounds (METRIC_RULES). If a sensor drops out (MISSING) or transmits a hardware spike (OUTLIER), the pipeline automatically imputes the value from the last verified physiological state and logs an audit entry.
  2. Centralized Time-Series Storage (PostgreSQL): Validated telemetry streams, crew profiles, flight surgeon accounts, hardware device registries, and medical alerts are persisted across structured tables (crew_telemetry, users, devices, notifications).
  3. Backend Orchestration & REST API (Java / Spring Boot): A Spring Boot service layer (VitalsService, ChcApiController, TelemetryController) exposes clean /api/... endpoints backed by Spring Data JPA repositories to serve live vitals, historical trends, and alert states.
  4. Clinical Dashboard & Autonomous Decision Engine (src/main/resources/static/): A mission-control web console tracks four core spaceflight health domains—Cardio (Heart Rate, SpO2, HRV), Bone (Bone Mineral Density, NTx, Urinary Calcium), Behaviour (Stress Index, Sleep Quality, Psychomotor Reaction Time), and Radiation (Dose Rate, Cumulative Mission Dose). When parameters drift, the engine computes severity levels, recommends targeted countermeasures, and updates crew readiness in real time.

Key Benefits

  • 100% Autonomous Offline Operation: Requires zero external cloud dependencies or third-party AI APIs. All clinical rules, anomaly detection, and triage logic execute locally onboard the spacecraft.
  • Resilience Against Sensor Noise: Automated boundary validation and state imputation prevent faulty wearable readings from triggering false alarms or corrupting medical records.
  • Actionable Clinical Guidance: Rather than displaying raw numbers alone, the interface translates physiological drift into immediate, step-by-step countermeasure protocols.
  • Role-Based Mission Workflows: Supports distinct operational views for astronauts monitoring personal readiness and Flight Surgeons reviewing crew-wide status and generating printable clinical briefs.

Intended Impact

  • Deep-Space Crew Autonomy: During Mars missions, one-way light-time communication delays reach 14+ minutes, making real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. ASTRAVITALS shifts immediate clinical triage directly onboard so crews can manage medical events independently.
  • Holistic Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Safety: Spacewalks carry compounding physiological risks. By cross-checking cardiovascular, skeletal, cognitive, and radiation thresholds simultaneously, the EVA Go/No-Go engine prevents astronauts from suiting up when subtle multi-system fatigue or radiation exposure compromises safety.
  • Terrestrial Telemedicine Transfer: Beyond spaceflight, the architecture is directly adaptable to isolated, bandwidth-constrained environments on Earth—including Antarctic research stations, submarines, maritime vessels, and remote rural clinics.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: Python 3, Java 17, SQL, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Backend Frameworks & Libraries: Java Spring Boot (Spring Web, Spring Data JPA), Python Flask, flask-cors, psycopg2.
  • Database: PostgreSQL (ASTRAVITALS relational and time-series schema).
  • Hardware & IoT Simulation: ESP32 microcontroller simulated via Wokwi, streaming multi-sensor biometric telemetry packets over HTTP/JSON.
  • Development & Build Tools: Apache Maven, IntelliJ IDEA, Git, and GitHub.

What Makes ASTRAVITALS Creative

  • Interactive ISS / Mars Latency Mode: Operators can toggle between Low Earth Orbit (0.2s delay) and Mars transit (14m 20s delay). Switching to Mars mode visually and functionally demonstrates communication blackout constraints, activating local autonomous triage protocols when ground control cannot respond in real time.
  • Cross-Domain EVA Go/No-Go Engine: Instead of evaluating vital signs in isolated silos, the decision engine synthesizes four distinct physiological systems into a unified operational clearance status (GO / CAUTION / NO-GO).
  • Self-Healing Biomedical Stream: Treating sensor reliability as a core clinical safety feature ensures continuous dashboard stability even during simulated hardware dropouts or packet corruption.

Design & Engineering Factors Considered

  • Communication Physics & Zero-Cloud Reliability: Because deep-space habitats cannot depend on external servers, we engineered a self-contained stack capable of running entirely on local habitat hardware.
  • Cognitive Load & Human Factors: Astronauts and flight controllers operate under high cognitive load. We designed a high-contrast dark-mode interface with clear visual hierarchy, color-coded thresholds, and concise action prompts to minimize interpretation time during emergencies.
  • Data Integrity & Auditability: Every imputed sensor reading and triggered medical alert is logged with timestamps and device identifiers so Flight Surgeons can distinguish true physiological anomalies from hardware artifacts during post-event reviews.
